fixture.interpretation: Fixture mode replays scripted replies for single_call and the three agent arms, with planted failures. Those rows check the ledger, policy and scorer; they are not model results. The non-LLM baselines call no model, so their fixture rows are real measurements on one noise stream per campaign.

live.interpretation: v1 live pilot on the v1 held-out family; non-LLM rows share the same noise streams.

live_v2.interpretation: v2 run A: pre-registered fixes, fresh held-out v2 family, same model as v1.

live_v2_sonnet.interpretation: v2 run B: second model, agent arm and tuned GP-UCB only, one run.

limitations: Synthetic response surfaces on a 66-candidate fictional simplex; no real materials data and no discovery claim.
The surrogate is a fixed-hyperparameter GP and the acquisition rule is textbook UCB; this is not a new optimisation algorithm.
Normalised regret uses the mean feasible value as the zero-skill reference; a campaign with no answer or an infeasible answer scores 1.0.
Fixture results for LLM arms are scripted and say nothing about model quality.

Each live run is 10 held-out campaigns at temperature 0 with one or two noise streams: an exploratory sample with min and max over runs, not a ranking. Episodes not run because a run cap was reached are reported as pending and excluded from denominators.
